digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI/CD — Gerrit Verified dispatch workflow
propositions: Gerrit Verified dispatch on main, not tickets-branch pushes, dominated GitHub Actions runner queue saturation on 2026-08-12/13, reaching 22 waiting jobs and 873s max runner wait time during incident-period peak.

Current Verified workflow executes 17 full-route runner jobs (peak 24 with mutation shards) with immediate 13-way fan-out, consuming up to 116 runner-minutes per patchset and creating repository-local queuing under Free plan 20-job concurrency limit.

Independent burst of three simultaneous full-route dispatches on 2026-08-15 created 22 waiting repository-local jobs within five minutes; organization-wide contention from other repositories is unobservable via Actions API but implies effective ceiling below stated 20-job limit.

Existing merged cancellation logic (4cbaa19315) eliminates most supersession waste; residual cross-patchset delay is 78-110s per rare replacement, insufficient to justify cross-change coalescing or debounce-induced vote delays.

Option A (bundle four always-on preflights + cap mutation at max-parallel: 3) reduces immediate fan-out from 13 to 10 and peak simultaneous demand from 19 to 12 while preserving all test coverage and diagnostic independence.

Option C (move macOS to branch-health schedule) delays macOS-specific regressions by up to six hours post-merge but frees one of five Free-plan macOS slots, achieving 9-11 minute pre-merge latency savings per run.
